sanskrit: evam uktvā muniśreṣṭham arudaṃ duḥkhito bhṛśam atha dhyātvā muhūrtaṃ tu bhagavān idam abravīt
english: Having spoken thus to that foremost of sages, I wept, greatly afflicted by grief. Then the blessed one, having reflected for a moment, spoke these words.

sanskrit: pakṣau ca te prapakṣau ca punar anyau bhaviṣyataḥ cakṣuṣī caiva prāṇāś ca vikramaś ca balaṃ ca te
english: "Your wings and secondary feathers shall grow anew; and likewise your eyes, your vitality, your valour, and your strength shall be restored to you."

sanskrit: purāṇe sumahat kāryaṃ bhaviṣyaṃ hi mayā śrutam dṛṣṭaṃ me tapasā caiva śrutvā ca viditaṃ mama
english: "For I have heard of a great deed yet to come, spoken of in ancient times; I have perceived it through my austerities, and it is known to me from what I have heard."

sanskrit: rājā daśaratho nāma kaś cid ikṣvākunandanaḥ tasya putro mahātejā rāmo nāma bhaviṣyati
english: "There is a king named Daśaratha, a scion of the Ikṣvāku dynasty; his son, of immense splendour, shall be named Rāma."

sanskrit: araṇyaṃ ca saha bhrātrā lakṣmaṇena gamiṣyati tasminn arthe niyuktaḥ san pitrā satyaparākramaḥ
english: "He, whose valour is true, being engaged in that task by his father, shall go to the forest along with his brother Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: nairṛto rāvaṇo nāma tasyā bhāryāṃ hariṣyati rākṣasendro janasthānād avadhyaḥ suradānavaiḥ
english: "Rāvaṇa, lord of the Rākṣasas, a demon by birth, invincible to gods and Dānavas, shall steal his wife from Janasthāna."

sanskrit: sā ca kāmaiḥ pralobhyantī bhakṣyair bhojyaiś ca maithilī na bhokṣyati mahābhāgā duḥkhamagnā yaśasvinī
english: "Though tempted with pleasures and with foods to eat and drink, the glorious Maithilī, that illustrious one, sunk in sorrow, shall not partake of them."

sanskrit: paramānnaṃ tu vaidehyā jñātvā dāsyati vāsavaḥ yad annam amṛtaprakhyaṃ surāṇām api durlabham
english: "But Vāsava, knowing Vaidehī's plight, shall give her food of the highest excellence — food akin to ambrosia and rare even among the gods."

sanskrit: tad annaṃ maithilī prāpya vijñāyendrād idaṃ tv iti agram uddhṛtya rāmāya bhūtale nirvapiṣyati
english: "Receiving that food and recognising it as coming from Indra, Maithilī shall take a portion from the top and scatter it on the ground as an offering to Rāma."

sanskrit: yadi jīvati me bhartā lakṣmaṇena saha prabhuḥ devatvaṃ gatayor vāpi tayor annam idaṃ tv iti
english: "Saying, 'If my lord, the master, still lives together with Lakṣmaṇa — or even if they have attained divinity — let this food be theirs.'"

sanskrit: eṣyanty anveṣakās tasyā rāmadūtāḥ plavaṃgamāḥ ākhyeyā rāmamahiṣī tvayā tebhyo vihaṃgama
english: "Leaping monkeys, serving as Rāma's messengers, shall come searching for her. You, O bird, must declare to them that she is Rāma's queen."

sanskrit: sarvathā tu na gantavyam īdṛśaḥ kva gamiṣyasi deśakālau pratīkṣasva pakṣau tvaṃ pratipatsyase
english: "In any case you must not go anywhere — where would one in your condition go? Wait for the right place and time; you shall regain your wings."

sanskrit: utsaheyam ahaṃ kartum adyaiva tvāṃ sapakṣakam ihasthas tvaṃ tu lokānāṃ hitaṃ kāryaṃ kariṣyasi
english: "I could restore your wings to you even today, but remaining here you shall accomplish a task beneficial to all the worlds."

sanskrit: tvayāpi khalu tat kāryaṃ tayoś ca nṛpaputrayoḥ brāhmaṇānāṃ surāṇāṃ ca munīnāṃ vāsavasya ca
english: "Indeed that task must be done by you — it is the task of those two princes, of the Brāhmaṇas, of the gods, of the sages, and of Vāsava himself."

sanskrit: icchāmy aham api draṣṭuṃ bhrātaru rāmalakṣmaṇau necche ciraṃ dhārayituṃ prāṇāṃs tyakṣye kalevaram
english: "I too wish to behold the brothers Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa; I do not wish to hold on to life much longer — I shall abandon this body."

sanskrit: etair anyaiś ca bahubhir vākyair vākyaviśāradaḥ māṃ praśasyābhyanujñāpya praviṣṭaḥ sa svam āśramam
english: With these and many other words, that master of speech, having praised me and granted me leave, entered his own hermitage.

sanskrit: kandarāt tu visarpitvā parvatasya śanaiḥ śanaiḥ ahaṃ vindhyaṃ samāruhya bhavataḥ pratipālaye
english: Creeping out of the cave of that mountain, slowly and gradually, I climbed the Vindhya and have been awaiting you here.

sanskrit: adya tv etasya kālasya sāgraṃ varṣaśataṃ gatam deśakālapratīkṣo 'smi hṛdi kṛtvā muner vacaḥ
english: And now more than a full hundred years of that time have passed; keeping the sage's words in my heart, I have been waiting for the right place and moment.

sanskrit: mahāprasthānam āsādya svargate tu niśākare māṃ nirdahati saṃtāpo vitarkair bahubhir vṛtam
english: After Niśākara undertook his great final journey and passed to heaven, grief consumes me, beset as I am by many apprehensions.

sanskrit: utthitāṃ maraṇe buddhiṃ muni vākyair nivartaye buddhir yā tena me dattā prāṇasaṃrakṣaṇāya tu sā me 'panayate duḥkhaṃ dīptevāgniśikhā tamaḥ
english: The resolve toward death that arises in me I turn back by means of the sage's words; the counsel he gave me for the preservation of my life dispels my sorrow as a blazing tongue of flame dispels darkness.

sanskrit: budhyatā ca mayā vīryaṃ rāvaṇasya durātmanaḥ putraḥ saṃtarjito vāgbhir na trātā maithilī katham
english: And knowing the might of evil-souled Rāvaṇa, his son was only threatened with words — why then was Maithilī not rescued?

sanskrit: tasyā vilapitaṃ śrutvā tau ca sītā vinākṛtau na me daśarathasnehāt putreṇotpāditaṃ priyam
english: Having heard her lament, and seeing those two bereft of Sītā, the son born out of Daśaratha's love for me did not perform what was dear to me.

sanskrit: tasya tv evaṃ bruvāṇasya saṃpāter vānaraiḥ saha utpetatus tadā pakṣau samakṣaṃ vanacāriṇām
english: And while Saṃpāti was speaking thus in the company of the monkeys, his two wings suddenly sprouted forth before the eyes of those forest-dwellers.

sanskrit: sa dṛṣṭvā svāṃ tanuṃ pakṣair udgatair aruṇacchadaiḥ praharṣam atulaṃ lebhe vānarāṃś cedam abravīt
english: Seeing his own body adorned with wings spread out and feathered with a reddish hue, he experienced incomparable joy and spoke these words to the monkeys.

sanskrit: niśākarasya maharṣeḥ prabhāvād amitātmanaḥ ādityaraśminirdagdhau pakṣau me punar utthitau
english: "By the power of the great sage Niśākara, of immeasurable soul, my wings, scorched by the rays of the sun, have grown again."

sanskrit: yauvane vartamānasya mamāsīd yaḥ parākramaḥ tam evādyāvagacchāmi balaṃ pauruṣam eva ca
english: "The valour I possessed in my youth — that very strength and manliness I perceive in myself today."

sanskrit: sarvathā kriyatāṃ yatnaḥ sītām adhigamiṣyatha pakṣalābho mamāyaṃ vaḥ siddhipratyaya kārakaḥ
english: "Strive by all means — you shall attain Sītā. This regaining of my wings is for you a token of certain success."

sanskrit: ity uktvā tān harīn sarvān saṃpātiḥ patatāṃ varaḥ utpapāta gireḥ śṛṅgāj jijñāsuḥ khagamo gatim
english: Having spoken thus to all those monkeys, Saṃpāti, foremost of fliers, leapt from the summit of the mountain, eager to test his movement through the sky.

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā prītisaṃhṛṣṭamānasāḥ babhūvur hariśārdūlā vikramābhyudayonmukhāḥ
english: Hearing his words, those tiger-like monkeys were overjoyed and delighted in their hearts, and turned their faces toward the rising of their prowess.

sanskrit: atha pavanasamānavikramāḥ plavagavarāḥ pratilabdha pauruṣāḥ abhijidabhimukhāṃ diśaṃ yayur janakasutā parimārgaṇonmukhāḥ
english: Then those best of leapers, with the swiftness of the wind, their manliness recovered, set out in the direction of Abhijit, eager to search for the daughter of Janaka.

sanskrit: ākhyātā gṛdhrarājena samutpatya plavaṃgamāḥ saṃgatāḥ prītisaṃyuktā vineduḥ siṃhavikramāḥ
english: Having been told by the king of vultures, the leaping monkeys sprang up together, filled with joy, and roared with the valour of lions.

sanskrit: saṃpāter vacanaṃ śrutvā harayo rāvaṇakṣayam hṛṣṭāḥ sāgaram ājagmuḥ sītādarśanakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
english: Having heard Saṃpāti's words regarding the destruction of Rāvaṇa, the joyful monkeys, eager to find Sītā, came to the ocean.

sanskrit: abhikramya tu taṃ deśaṃ dadṛśur bhīmavikramāḥ kṛtsnaṃ lokasya mahataḥ pratibimbam iva sthitam
english: Approaching that place, those monkeys of awesome valour beheld it — standing as if it were a reflection of the entire great world.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇasya samudrasya samāsādyottarāṃ diśam saṃniveśaṃ tataś cakruḥ sahitā vānarottamāḥ
english: Having reached the northern shore of the southern ocean, those foremost of monkeys then encamped together.

sanskrit: sattvair mahadbhir vikṛtaiḥ krīḍadbhir vividhair jale vyāttāsyaiḥ sumahākāyair ūrmibhiś ca samākulam
english: They saw the ocean thronged with immense and monstrous creatures of various kinds sporting in the water, with gaping mouths and enormous bodies, and filled with surging waves.

sanskrit: prasuptam iva cānyatra krīḍantam iva cānyataḥ kva cit parvatamātraiś ca jalarāśibhir āvṛtam
english: In some places it seemed as if asleep, in other places as if at play, and here and there it was surrounded by masses of water as vast as mountains.

sanskrit: saṃkulaṃ dānavendraiś ca pātālatalavāsibhiḥ romaharṣakaraṃ dṛṣṭvā viṣeduḥ kapikuñjarāḥ
english: Seeing it crowded with great Dānava lords dwelling in the depths of Pātāla, a sight that made the hair stand on end, those elephant-like monkeys fell into despondency.

sanskrit: ākāśam iva duṣpāraṃ sāgaraṃ prekṣya vānarāḥ viṣeduḥ sahasā sarve kathaṃ kāryam iti bruvan
english: Gazing at the ocean, which seemed as uncrossable as the sky itself, all the monkeys suddenly fell into despair, saying, "How shall the task be accomplished?"

sanskrit: viṣaṇṇāṃ vāhinīṃ dṛṣṭvā sāgarasya nirīkṣaṇāt āśvāsayām āsa harīn bhayārtān harisattamaḥ
english: Seeing the army thus cast into despondency by the sight of the ocean, the foremost of monkeys consoled those monkeys who were afflicted by fear.

sanskrit: na niṣādena naḥ kāryaṃ viṣādo doṣavattaraḥ viṣādo hanti puruṣaṃ bālaṃ kruddha ivoragaḥ
english: "We have no need of despair; despondency is the greater fault. Despondency destroys a person as an enraged serpent destroys a child."

sanskrit: viṣādo 'yaṃ prasahate vikrame paryupasthite tejasā tasya hīnasya puruṣārtho na sidhyati
english: "This despondency overpowers one when the moment for valiant action arrives; stripped of its energy, the purpose of man cannot be achieved."

sanskrit: tasyāṃ rātryāṃ vyatītāyām aṅgado vānaraiḥ saha harivṛddhaiḥ samāgamya punar mantram amantrayat
english: When that night had passed, Aṅgada convened another counsel together with the monkeys, assembling with the elder leaders of the monkey host.

sanskrit: sā vānarāṇāṃ dhvajinī parivāryāṅgadaṃ babhau vāsavaṃ parivāryeva marutāṃ vāhinī sthitā
english: That army of monkeys, surrounding Aṅgada, stood resplendent — even as the host of Maruts stands surrounding Vāsava.

sanskrit: ko 'nyas tāṃ vānarīṃ senāṃ śaktaḥ stambhayituṃ bhavet anyatra vālitanayād anyatra ca hanūmataḥ
english: "Who else would be capable of steadying that monkey army other than the son of Vālin and other than Hanūmat?"

sanskrit: tatas tān harivṛddhāṃś ca tac ca sainyam ariṃdamaḥ anumānyāṅgadaḥ śrīmān vākyam arthavad abravīt
english: Then the glorious Aṅgada, the subduer of foes, having paid his respects to those elder monkeys and to the army, spoke words full of purpose.

sanskrit: ka idānīṃ mahātejā laṅghayiṣyati sāgaram kaḥ kariṣyati sugrīvaṃ satyasaṃdham ariṃdamam
english: "Who among you, O mighty one, shall now leap over the ocean? Who shall fulfil the purpose of Sugrīva, true to his pledge and the subduer of enemies?"

sanskrit: ko vīro yojanaśataṃ laṅghayeta plavagarṣabhāḥ imāṃś ca yūthapān sarvān mocayet ko mahābhayāt
english: "What hero, O best of leapers, could vault a hundred yojanas? Who could deliver all these troop leaders from this great peril?"

sanskrit: kasya prasādād dārāṃś ca putrāṃś caiva gṛhāṇi ca ito nivṛttāḥ paśyema siddhārthāḥ sukhino vayam
english: "By whose grace, having turned back from here with our purpose accomplished, might we joyfully see again our wives, our children, and our homes?"

sanskrit: kasya prasādād rāmaṃ ca lakṣmaṇaṃ ca mahābalam abhigacchema saṃhṛṣṭāḥ sugrīvaṃ ca mahābalam
english: "By whose grace might we joyfully approach Rāma and the mighty Lakṣmaṇa, and the mighty Sugrīva?"

sanskrit: yadi kaś cit samartho vaḥ sāgaraplavane hariḥ sa dadātv iha naḥ śīghraṃ puṇyām abhayadakṣiṇām
english: "If any monkey among you is capable of crossing the ocean, let him quickly grant us here the auspicious gift of fearlessness."

sanskrit: aṅgadasya vacaḥ śrutvā na kaś cit kiṃ cid abravīt stimitevābhavat sarvā sā tatra harivāhinī
english: Having heard Aṅgada's words, not one of them said anything; that entire monkey army stood there motionless as if frozen.

sanskrit: punar evāṅgadaḥ prāha tān harīn harisattamaḥ sarve balavatāṃ śreṣṭhā bhavanto dṛḍhavikramāḥ
english: Again Aṅgada, foremost of monkeys, addressed those monkeys: "You are all the foremost of the powerful, of steadfast valour."

sanskrit: vyapadeśya kule jātāḥ pūjitāś cāpy abhīkṣṇaśaḥ na hi vo gamane saṃgaḥ kadā cid api kasya cit
english: "You are born in distinguished lineages and are honoured repeatedly; there is no obstacle for any of you, at any time, in going across."

sanskrit: bruvadhvaṃ yasya yā śaktir gamane plavagarṣabhāḥ
english: "Declare, O best of leapers, whatever capacity each of you has for making the crossing."
